chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from one of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Nothing comes forth from the presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until it begins with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then with Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, then with each one after another, so that our last should not be more knowledgeable than our first.

key_terms.آخِرُنَا: our last, referring to the later Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.أَعْلَمَ: more knowledgeable, denoting superiority in knowledge
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, the next recipient after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.أَوَّلِنَا: our first, referring to the earlier Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the Divine source from whom the matter proceeds
key_terms.بِوَاحِدٍ بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ: one after another, indicating sequential transmission
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, first recipient in the sequence

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the transmission of divine knowledge to the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that what proceeds from Allah عزّ وجلّ is conveyed first to Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and then successively to each Imam. It emphasizes the ordered transmission of divine knowledge and the continuity of authority and knowledge among the Imams عليهم السلام.
